one_line: Email-first accountable AI teammates that coordinate governed work asynchronously.
what_it_does: Creates role-based AI specialists connected to approved company systems, with dashboard/email entry and replay-safe governed execution.
leverage_rationale: Shared governed queue, approved system access, replay safety, and asynchronous execution make the agent workforce substantially more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes a shared dashboard/email entry into one replay-safe queue and governed runtime.
Frame sheet shows AI teammate configuration and an accountable teammate-at-work workspace.
execution_rationale: The product surfaces a coherent email-to-workspace workflow and visible configuration/activity surfaces, though the frame sheet is largely marketing/storyboard imagery and does not prove a complete task end to end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows teammate setup, connected service/status rows, and a secure workspace view.
Demo is reported alive and a public repository is present.
impact_rationale: Small-business operators and teams lacking dedicated AI operations support have a concrete management and coordination problem; the proposed accountable workforce addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Description identifies context carrying, model coordination, quota recovery, and result reconciliation as user pain points.
Email-first familiar workflow and approval/accountability framing are visible in the frames.
creativity_rationale: The combination of email-native AI teammates, governed company addresses, and asynchronous accountable execution is a fresh and ambitious agent-workforce synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Concept treats AI systems as role-based company teammates rather than a single chat assistant.
Frame messaging emphasizes secure links and an accountable teammate at work.
usability_note: Familiar email entry and a secure workspace suggest strong usability, but no live hands-on usability evidence is available.
red_flags: Frame sheet is mostly repeated promotional views; exact tool invocation and completed output are not legible.
standouts: Email-first accountable AI workforce concept.
Governed, replay-safe shared runtime.
advance_reason: Strong concept and credible product surfaces with an alive demo; execution evidence is good but not fully end-to-end.

one_line: A guided Arduino workbench where an agent inspects and corrects a beginner's live circuit.
what_it_does: Teaches six Arduino projects through a simulated breadboard, with WebMCP tools for explanation, inspection, pointing, wiring changes, verification, and tests.
leverage_rationale: The page-native tools expose exact breadboard state and allow precise correction/testing; screenshot-based or generic UI automation would be markedly less reliable for wiring semantics.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly contrasts WebMCP with screenshot guessing and says the agent sees the same bench.
Frame sheet shows the smart parking barrier build, agent activity marker, and status coach.
execution_rationale: The visible workbench combines chapters, parts, wiring, simulation, code/status, and agent feedback into a coherent learning workflow; the video demonstrates product motion and state, though exact test completion is not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a populated smart parking barrier circuit/workbench across states.
Description lists six chapters and a functional test workflow; demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Arduino beginners have a specific, common debugging and learning problem, and live circuit inspection can reduce frustrating first-hour failures while teaching the reason for corrections.
impact_evidence: Description identifies wrong holes, leads, and insufficient PDF guidance as the target problem.
Visible instructional steps, circuit simulation, and agent coach support the learner workflow.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP to ground an educational agent in the exact semantic state of a breadboard, including a controlled mutation tool, is memorable and well matched to the medium.
creativity_evidence: Agent can inspect, point at, attach/pull leads, and run chapter-specific tests.
Frame sheet visibly communicates agent activity rather than only presenting a chatbot.
usability_note: Stepwise chapters, visual pointing, and explicit activity states are promising for beginners; actual learner usability is not independently tested.
red_flags: Exact final test result is not clearly legible in the contact sheet.
standouts: Exceptional live-state grounding for electronics education.
Agent actions are made visible and pedagogically meaningful.
advance_reason: Best-in-packet WebMCP leverage with clear product motion, strong audience fit, and a coherent demonstrated workflow.

one_line: A fertility journey workspace where agents find authorized matches and prepare human-reviewed introductions.
what_it_does: Unifies journey status, candidate search/profile access, and draft introductions while keeping consequential fertility decisions with humans.
leverage_rationale: Tools close over signed-in journey and authorization state, returning only permitted candidate details and preparing actions in the same interface; generic automation would be less safe and context-precise.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies live journey context, authorized candidate filtering, and a non-submitting introduction preparation tool.
Frame sheet shows shared journey, page-defined tools, and agent workspace messaging.
execution_rationale: The product presents a coherent dashboard-to-directory-to-review workflow and clear human-control boundary, but the frame evidence is primarily conceptual and does not show a legible completed introduction flow.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows agent workspace framing and unified messages/files/calendars/handoffs concept.
Demo is reported alive and the packet describes purpose-built tools.
impact_rationale: Fertility journeys are high-stakes, fragmented, and emotionally important; a controlled shared workspace that clarifies next steps and authorized matching has substantial value for its specific audience.
impact_evidence: Description names intended parents, surrogates, donors, and reviewers and the fragmented coordination problem.
Human review is preserved for consequential decisions.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native shared context and authorization-aware preparation to fertility coordination is an ambitious, sensitive, and distinctive interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tools are designed around the user's current journey and candidate-access permissions.
Frame messaging emphasizes one shared journey and page-defined tools.
usability_note: A single journey workspace should reduce fragmentation, but the stakes and login requirement make clarity and safeguards critical.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not clearly show candidate search or introduction preparation end to end.
High-stakes domain requires stronger evidence of privacy and authorization behavior.
standouts: Strong human-control design for a high-stakes workflow.
Context- and authorization-aware agent surface.
advance_reason: High-impact, differentiated concept with plausible shared-state execution, despite only partial visual proof.

one_line: An agent prepares code-review findings inline while reviewers retain publication judgment.
what_it_does: Reviews pull requests or queues, surfaces findings beside changed lines, and keeps every finding private until a human approves or dismisses it.
leverage_rationale: Structured PR context and inline draft findings improve reliability and shared reviewer state, but a general agent with GitHub access could achieve much of the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description says findings are placed directly below changed lines and remain private drafts.
Frame sheet shows a review queue and prepared review cards, but not legible tool calls.
execution_rationale: The queue, inline findings, and approval boundary form a coherent review product, with video evidence of queue states; the actual GitHub end-to-end path is not fully visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows review queue cards and prepared-review positioning.
Description details both demo-web and GitHub extension surfaces; demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Code review is a real, high-leverage attention bottleneck, and reducing mechanical scanning without removing reviewer ownership offers clear value to software teams.
impact_evidence: Description identifies sustained attention, context tracing, and noisy bot comments as the problem.
Human approval/dismissal and no-findings triage directly address review burden.
creativity_rationale: Human-owned, inline draft review is a thoughtful synthesis rather than a novel category, with a meaningful interaction distinction between agent preparation and reviewer judgment.
creativity_evidence: Every finding starts private and must be approved or dismissed.
Queue organization and inline contextual findings pursue the human-in-the-loop idea deeply.
usability_note: Inline context and private drafts are well suited to reviewer workflow; extension and demo surfaces may add setup complexity.
red_flags: Exact agent invocation and posted-result state are not legible in the frames.
standouts: Strong preservation of human judgment.
Findings appear in the normal review context rather than a separate chat.
advance_reason: Clear useful workflow with solid visible queue evidence and a credible human-review safety model.

one_line: A voxel data-center builder and standards simulator operated by an agent through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Lets users build facilities in a 3D voxel grid, simulate operations, score against standards, and generate manifests/certification while limiting agent exposure.
leverage_rationale: A structured page-native surface can manipulate spatial infrastructure, run deterministic standards checks, and expose privacy-preserving verdicts more precisely than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Description lists agent construction, standards checking, schema-manifest generation, simulation, and certification steps.
Frame sheet shows a browser 3D grid, changing scene views, a right-side execution/log panel, and a newly visible object.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence shows a functioning 3D scene and apparent agent/log progression, but the submitted demo is reported dead and the exact construction, simulation, and certification outputs are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows progressive 3D scene states and an execution/log panel.
Demo is reported dead, despite a public repository and detailed scope description.
impact_rationale: Facility designers, operators, and auditors have a real need for deterministic compliance and operational estimates, especially where sensitive layouts should not be disclosed.
impact_evidence: Description targets PUE, cooling, layout, staffing, carbon, water, and international standards.
Zero-knowledge verdict/public certification framing addresses confidentiality concerns.
creativity_rationale: The combination of Lego-like voxel facility design, standards simulation, privacy-preserving certification, and constrained agent knowledge is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Concept unifies a 3D builder, SimCity-like facilities simulation, 37 cited rules, and zero-knowledge proof framing.
Agent privacy is treated as the same problem as design confidentiality.
usability_note: The visual builder may be approachable, but the complexity of standards and the dead demo materially limit confidence in practical usability.
red_flags: Most log text and final certification output are not readable in the frame sheet.
standouts: Most ambitious concept in the packet.
Privacy-preserving compliance angle is distinctive.
advance_reason: Exceptional ambition and leverage concept, but dead live demo and incomplete visible end state reduce execution confidence.

one_line: A shared canvas where humans and agents co-create diagrams, notes, and linked ideas.
what_it_does: Provides a real-time canvas with notes, SVG links, Copilot interaction, and browser-native WebMCP status/connection surfaces.
leverage_rationale: Agent-native manipulation of shared diagram state and links can be more structured and repeatable than generic UI driving, though the core canvas outcome remains possible through automation.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes human and AI co-creation in the same live workspace.
Frame evidence includes a WebMCP status monitor, exposed browser tools, agent connections, Copilot drawer, and linked canvas nodes.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent canvas, notes, links, Copilot, and protocol/status layers with multiple real screenshots, but does not clearly demonstrate a complete agent-created artifact in motion.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet/gallery descriptions show settings/status monitor, Copilot drawer, and multi-node dynamic SVG links.
Demo is reported alive and a public repository is present.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals brainstorming and planning can benefit from a shared visual workspace that reduces the gap between agent suggestions and editable structure.
impact_evidence: Description identifies brainstorming, structuring ideas, and project planning as the audience/use case.
Visible canvas and notes workflow supports collaborative organization.
creativity_rationale: Treating the canvas as a shared human-agent co-working surface, with explicit protocol observability, is a fresh and well-expressed interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Frame descriptions show a four-stage map of human touchpoints and eliminated pain points.
Dynamic SVG links and agent connections are integrated into the canvas concept.
usability_note: Visual canvas collaboration is intuitive, but agent controls and protocol monitoring could add cognitive load.
red_flags: Exact tool invocation and end-to-end agent artifact creation are not legible.
standouts: Strong shared-state canvas framing.
Protocol observability is presented as part of the product.
advance_reason: Coherent, visually evidenced collaborative product with a meaningful agent-native interaction model.

one_line: An in-page trust catalog that lets agents check whether newly exposed tools are safe to use.
what_it_does: Curates tools with source-backed trust/fit/ease/reliability/reach/cost assessments and exposes the catalog through WebMCP for mid-task verification.
leverage_rationale: The product addresses a uniquely WebMCP-timed decision: an agent can inspect trust information in-page at the moment a page hands it a tool, rather than relying on prior configuration.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly positions Vettory as callable in-page through WebMCP and asks whether a tool is safe right now.
Frame sheet shows the trust-warning story, email-like tool, and inspection/developer panel, though exact calls are not legible.
execution_rationale: The catalog, rubric, verdicts, and deceptive-email demonstration form a focused coherent MVP; frame progression shows the app and inspection context but not a fully legible verdict flow.
execution_evidence: Description states 22 curated tools, source-backed claims, and trusted/caution/warning verdicts.
Frame sheet shows transition from warning landing page to mailbox/tool inspection UI; demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Tool supply-chain and data-exfiltration risk is a real problem for agent users, and an accessible trust check could prevent harmful actions without requiring a large catalog.
impact_evidence: Description gives a concrete malicious-package/BCC scenario and explains why WebMCP makes the question immediate.
Visible warning framing and email inspection workflow make the risk understandable.
creativity_rationale: A deliberately small, source-backed trust layer for tools offered dynamically by webpages is a novel and highly memorable response to an emerging WebMCP-specific risk.
creativity_evidence: The concept asks agents to verify trust during the task, not at installation time.
Six-part published evaluation rubric and exclusion of unresolved material risks show depth.
usability_note: Small curated scope and simple verdicts are approachable, though trust judgments must remain understandable and current.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not clearly show a final trust verdict or tool-call response.
standouts: Strong WebMCP-native security thesis.
Concrete adversarial demo makes the problem legible.
advance_reason: Distinctive, timely agent-safety product with strong concept and credible visible implementation.

one_line: An agentic virtual-college planner for comparing degree paths and checking transcript feasibility.
what_it_does: Uses shared functions and WebMCP tools to compare programs, select tracks, check prerequisites against transcripts, and record human/agent actions.
leverage_rationale: Typed shared functions and live academic data improve precision and shared state, but general agents could perform much of the planning with UI access and database-backed forms.
leverage_evidence: Description says human UI and WebMCP callbacks invoke the same real functions and persist to MongoDB.
Frame sheet shows changing academic selectors, course lists, and planning states, but no legible tool log.
execution_rationale: The visible app has a coherent course-planning interface with selections and expanded data, and the packet describes two concrete decision workflows; end-to-end feasibility results are not clearly shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows dropdown selection and changing planning panels.
Public repository is present; demo status is unknown.
impact_rationale: Prospective students and upperclassmen face real degree-path and prerequisite decisions; a planner grounded in transcript state can provide credible guidance.
impact_evidence: Description names prospective students comparing programs and upperclassmen checking specialization feasibility.
Visible interface is clearly a course/degree planning application.
creativity_rationale: The shared human-agent state, attributable session log, and feasibility-checking workflow add a meaningful angle to a known academic-planning category.
creativity_evidence: Agent-authored notes/conflict flags are described as distinct from human plan entries.
Same functions serve human and agent paths.
usability_note: Structured selectors and shared logs can support advising, though academic data complexity may make the interface dense.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not visibly prove a feasibility result or readable agent session log.
standouts: Shared function path for human and agent actions.
Concrete transcript-aware decision point.
advance_reason: Useful, coherent education workflow with visible application state changes, though WebMCP-specific proof is partial.

what_it_does: Displays aerial imagery and selected buildings while page-native tools analyze population exposure, road access, and critical facilities in live map state.
leverage_rationale: Viewport-scoped tools resolve the ambiguity of 'here' by closing over live map state; a remote/general agent would need brittle manual reconstruction of coordinates and selection.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly contrasts page-native tools with remote MCP lacking viewport and selection context.
Frame sheet shows a map console with persistent side panels and a changed coastal/urban viewport.
execution_rationale: The map console and changing viewport are clearly demonstrated, and the described use case is coherent, but no legible analysis result or selected-building workflow is visible in the contact sheet.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows repeated operational map states and a clear zoom/pan change.
Demo is reported alive and a public repository is present.
impact_rationale: Emergency responders and post-disaster analysts have an urgent, specific triage problem; combining imagery with population, roads, and critical-facility context can materially improve decisions.
impact_evidence: Description grounds the product in first-72-hours disaster triage.
Named outputs directly answer operational questions about exposure and access.
creativity_rationale: Making 'here' a first-class, live page context for agent analysis is a precise and compelling interaction model for geospatial emergency work.
creativity_evidence: Tools are scoped to viewport, selected building, and imagery date rather than free-floating parameters.
The WebMCP-vs-server-MCP argument is embodied in the product model.
usability_note: Viewport-grounded questions should reduce coordinate friction, though crisis operators need highly legible status and results.
red_flags: No readable analysis result or tool invocation appears in the frame sheet.
Most screenshots show little state change beyond viewport movement.
standouts: Excellent demonstration of live UI context as agent input.
High-value disaster-response audience and use case.
advance_reason: Very strong leverage and impact thesis with a visibly real map console; result evidence is incomplete.

one_line: A browser-native pre-flight gate for inspecting and safely cleaning one granted agent workspace.
what_it_does: Scans allowlisted configuration/package/instruction metadata, explains drift with an evidence graph, and applies approved reversible cleanup with explicit browser permission.
leverage_rationale: A page-native, explicitly scoped workspace boundary and reversible supervised writes provide structured state, provenance, and safety that generic UI automation would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies one explicitly granted workspace, read-only first pass, evidence graph, supervised plan, and reversible cleanup.
Frame sheet shows a dark 3D/editor-like workspace with an execution/log panel and state changes, consistent with inspected agent tooling.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a reproducible scan-to-findings-to-approved-cleanup flow with explicit permissions and the frame sequence shows product state and execution monitoring; exact finding text is not legible.
execution_evidence: Description states the demo scans seeded duplicate entries, invalid endpoint, and disabled server, then creates a hardening plan and performs approved cleanup.
Demo is reported alive and a public repository is present.
impact_rationale: Agent configuration drift and hidden inherited instructions are real developer problems; a readable pre-flight report and safe cleanup can prevent surprising runs.
impact_evidence: Description names duplicate servers, invalid endpoints, disabled entries, package drift, and layered instructions.
Explicit grant/approval/write-permission steps target real operational risk.
creativity_rationale: The browser-native pre-flight gate turns MCP configuration hygiene into a shared, inspectable agent workflow without an installed server, with evidence-linked findings and reversible writes.
creativity_evidence: Product defines a focused new DevTools category around agent readiness.
Evidence graph and supervised reversible cleanup are more distinctive than a generic config editor.
usability_note: Read-only first pass, concrete findings, and explicit write permission support safe use; workspace granting may still be technical.
red_flags: Frame text is too small to verify exact findings or cleanup result.
The product is explicitly an MVP.
standouts: Strong safety and provenance boundary.
Reversible cleanup with human approval is unusually well specified.
advance_reason: Focused, credible developer workflow with strong safety design and described end-to-end behavior.
